project.name: stylo
project.description: The Stylo CSS engine. A high-performance, browser-grade CSS style engine written in Rust that powers Servo and Firefox.

nodes.name: appearance_base_rule.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the @appearance-base CSS rule for user-agent stylesheet appearance-dependent styles, wrapping nested CSS rules with memory measurement, CSS serialization, and deep cloning support.
nodes.languageNotes: Gated behind #[cfg(feature = "gecko")] for heap size measurement.

nodes.name: AppearanceBaseRule
nodes.summary: Represents an @appearance-base rule containing nested CSS rules and source location, with support for heap size measurement, CSS serialization via ToCssWithGuard, and deep cloning via DeepCloneWithLock.

nodes.name: container_rule.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the CSS @container rule from CSS Containment Level 3, providing container query parsing, container-name matching, container size query evaluation, and traversal of the element tree to find query containers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a TraversalResult enum for tree walking with InProgress/StopTraversal/Done states, and a lazy evaluation pattern via ContainerSizeQuery's NotEvaluated/Evaluated variants.

nodes.name: ContainerRule
nodes.summary: Represents a parsed @container CSS rule with container conditions, nested rules, and source location, with heap measurement, deep cloning, and CSS serialization support.

nodes.name: ContainerCondition
nodes.summary: Combines a container name filter with an optional query condition and pre-computed feature flags for efficient container matching against elements in the DOM tree.

nodes.name: ContainerInfo
nodes.summary: Information needed to evaluate an individual container query, including the container's physical size, writing mode, and inherited style reference.

nodes.name: ContainerSizeQueryResult
nodes.summary: Result of a container size query holding optional width and height in app units, with methods to resolve logical dimensions and merge results from multiple container lookups.

nodes.name: for_element
nodes.summary: Creates a new ContainerSizeQuery for a given element, with deferred ancestor traversal that optionally checks the parent style for the size container flag.

nodes.name: for_option_element
nodes.summary: Creates a ContainerSizeQuery for an optional element, returning a none query if the element is absent.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the result of a container size query, performing the deferred lookup on first call and caching the evaluated result.

nodes.name: document_rule.rs

nodes.name: DocumentRule

nodes.name: DocumentCondition

nodes.name: stylist.rs
nodes.summary: Core CSS selector matching and style computation engine for Servo/Gecko. Manages stylesheets across origins (user-agent, user, author), maintains cascade data structures with invalidation maps and rule trees, and provides the primary API for pushing applicable declarations and resolving computed styles for elements and pseudo-elements.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust implementation using Servo's selectors crate for CSS selector matching. Employs generics with TElement trait for cross-engine (Servo/Gecko) compatibility. Uses reference-counted Arcs and shared locks for thread-safe stylesheet management.

nodes.name: CascadeDataDifference

nodes.name: DocumentCascadeData
nodes.summary: Aggregates CascadeData for all three origins (user-agent, user, author) into a single document-level structure. Provides origin-iterators and rebuild orchestration during stylesheet flushing.

nodes.name: Stylist
nodes.summary: Central struct holding all selectors and device characteristics for a document. Owns stylesheets, rule tree, cascade data per origin, custom property registrations, and the computation device. Created once per pipeline and rebuilt when stylesheets or device constraints change.

nodes.name: PageRuleMap
nodes.summary: Stores and matches @page rules indexed by page name. Provides matching logic that considers page-name selectors and pseudo-class flags to find applicable page rules in layer order.

nodes.name: ExtraStyleData
nodes.summary: Holds effective at-rule style data extracted from stylesheets: @font-face, @font-feature-values, @font-palette-values, @counter-style, @position-try, @page, and @view-transition rules. All entries are layer-ordered for correct cascade resolution.

nodes.summary: Steals the free list from the root node, iterates all nodes in it, and drops those whose refcount reaches zero after decrementing, using acquire/release semantics for safe concurrent memory reclamation.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand Stylo's purpose as a high-performance CSS style engine written in Rust that powers both Servo and Firefox. This document maps the crate architecture, explains the branching strategy (spidermonkey, gecko, servo), and provides essential context for how the major subsystems -- the style crate, selectors library, and support crates -- fit together.

tour.title: Crate Entry Point & Workspace
tour.description: The workspace manifest (Cargo.toml) defines 11 member crates spanning the style engine, selector library, shared utilities, and procedural macros. The crate root (lib.rs) re-exports every public subsystem, giving you a bird's-eye view of the entire engine: from the stylist and matching modules through values, properties, and selectors. Every subsystem you will explore in later steps is declared here as a public module.

tour.title: CSS Selector Engine
tour.description: The selectors crate is a standalone library for parsing and matching CSS selectors according to the Selectors Level 4 specification. At 4923 lines, parser.rs is one of the largest files in the project and handles every selector type from simple type selectors through complex combinators, pseudo-classes, pseudo-elements, and :where/:is/:not specificity. The matching.rs module then evaluates parsed selectors against DOM elements, implementing the core boolean logic and specificity computation that determines whether a selector applies.
tour.languageLesson: The parser.rs file uses Rust's recursive descent parsing pattern extensively, matching on token streams to build a Selector AST. The matching.rs module leverages trait-based polymorphism through the SelectorImpl trait, allowing the same matching engine to work with different browser backends (Servo vs Gecko) without duplicating logic.

tour.title: Cascade Rule Tree
tour.description: The cascade rule tree organizes CSS declarations by the three axes of the cascade: origin (author, user, user-agent), specificity, and source order. Each node in the tree represents a unique combination of these axes, and declarations are stored in a garbage-collected structure that allows efficient insertion and lookup during style recalculation. The rule tree is central to performance: it avoids duplicating computed data across elements that share the same cascade path.
tour.languageLesson: The rule tree uses a custom unsafe_box for interior mutability and a mark-sweep GC pattern. The tree is built from multiple sub-modules (core.rs, level.rs, map.rs, source.rs) that each handle one aspect of cascade management, demonstrating Rust's module-level decomposition around a single abstraction.

tour.title: Style Resolution Pipeline
tour.description: The Stylist is the central orchestrator of the style engine: it holds the stylesheet collection, manages the selector map for efficient lookup, and dispatches matching requests for each element. The matching module ties together the DOM abstractions -- the TElement and TNode traits from dom.rs -- with traversal context from context.rs to perform full style resolution. After matching, the StyleAdjuster applies fixups for writing modes, display types, and other properties that depend on the computed values of other properties, completing the pipeline from raw DOM to fully styled element.
tour.languageLesson: The TElement and TNode traits in dom.rs are the primary abstraction boundary of the engine. They define the DOM contract using associated types and trait methods, allowing the same matching and styling logic to work with Servo's DOM (servo/mod.rs) and Firefox's DOM via FFI (gecko/wrapper.rs) without changing the core algorithm.

tour.title: CSS Values & Property System
tour.description: CSS values flow through three distinct representations: specified values (as written in the stylesheet), computed values (resolved for layout), and animated values (interpolated between states). The values module barrel re-exports all value types organized into specified/, computed/, animated/, and generics/ sub-modules. The property system defines the property ID registry, declaration blocks that hold property-value pairs, and the cascading logic that merges declarations from multiple sources. The color module handles modern CSS color syntax including OKLab, display-p3, and relative color syntax, which feeds into both the values and properties systems.
tour.languageLesson: The values system uses a three-phase architecture (specified -> computed -> animated) common to all browser engines. Each phase is a separate sub-module with its own type representations. The generics/ sub-module contains parameterized value types (e.g., GenericLength, GenericTransform) that are instantiated with either specified or computed representations, using Rust's generics to avoid code duplication.

tour.title: Browser Integration & Style Invalidation
tour.description: The Gecko wrapper (2267 lines) implements the TElement trait using Firefox's internal DOM representation accessed via FFI, allowing the engine to run inside Firefox without modifying its core algorithm. The Servo animation module handles CSS animations and transitions with Servo-specific types for keyframe and transition management. The invalidation map tracks dependency relationships between elements, classes, attributes, and states so the engine knows exactly which elements need restyling when something changes -- avoiding full re-traversals. The stylesheet rules module defines the master CssRule enum that dispatches to all @-rule types (@import, @media, @container, @keyframes, etc.), forming the backbone of the stylesheet subsystem.
tour.languageLesson: The Gecko FFI layer uses #[repr(C)] structs and extern "C" function declarations to bridge Rust and C++. The wrapper.rs file demonstrates the adapter pattern at scale: it implements the pure-Rust TElement trait by translating calls into Gecko's C++ DOM API, handling reference counting, thread safety, and memory layout differences between the two runtimes.
